paragraphs.text: Make Cmd+K open a Spotlight-style session palette instead of focusing the sidebar search box — with
in-place renaming and up to three tags per session.
# dsh-plugin-session-palette
Press ⌘K and get a **Spotlight-style session palette** instead of a search box in the corner — recen
t first, running and waiting sessions on top, a preview of each session's **last turn** before you c
ommit to opening it, two ways to **rename a session in place** — ⌘⇧R on the highlighted row, or a **
double click on the title** at the top of an open conversation — and **tags**: up to three per sessi
on, clickable to filter.
> dsh-plugin-session-palette — ⌘K 弹出会话面板：最近优先，正在运行与等待你的置顶，预览最后一个 turn，⌘⇧R 或双击标题就地改名，还能给会话打标签（最多 3 个，
lugin-session-palette — ⌘K 弹出会话面板：最近优先，正在运行与等待你的置顶，预览最后一个 turn，⌘⇧R 或双击标题就地改名，还能给会话打标签（最多 3 个，点标签就筛选）
中文说明（点开） —— ⌘K 从「聚焦侧边栏搜索框」变成「蹦出一个会话面板」
**它是什么**：DSH Web 客户端的会话切换器。按 ⌘K，屏幕上方弹出一个面板：左边是会话列表（按「需要你 / 活跃 / 今天 / 昨天 / 过去 7 天 / 过去 30 天 / 更早」分组），
右边是高亮那条的预览——包含它最后一个 turn 的**你的提问**和**模型回复**。方向键选，回车进。
**为什么做**：DSH 原本的 ⌘K 是「展开侧边栏 → 展开搜索框 → 把焦点丢进左下角那个输入框」。要切换会话，视线得从正文移到屏幕角落，而且只能看到一个平铺列表。VS Code 的 ⌘P、Su
blime 的 ⌘P、macOS 的 ⌘空格 都是把它做成**视线所在处弹出的浮层**——因为切换会话是高频动作，值得一次专门的界面。
**四个视图**（Tab 向前循环、⇧Tab 向后）：
| 视图 | 回答的问题 | 内容 |
[该节后续省略]
## Why
DSH's ⌘K expands the sidebar, expands the search field, un-collapses the rail if needed, and *then*
focuses the input — with a 300 ms delay when the rail has to slide open first. Switching sessions is
a high-frequency action, and the cost lands in the worst place: your eyes have to leave the convers
ation and find a field in the corner.
Every tool that solves this well solves it the same way — VS Code, Sublime, Spotlight — with an over
lay at the point of attention. This is that overlay.
The second problem is ordering. The host sorts sessions by `updatedAt`, which is `max(createdAt, las
tPromptAt)`: **the last time the user wrote**, not the last time anything happened. An agent reply d
oes not move it. So a session whose agent just finished, or one that is blocked waiting for your app
roval, can sit below a dozen conversations you merely touched more recently. The palette ranks *live
state* above the clock — waiting on you, then running, then finished-but-unread — and only then fal
ls back to recency buckets.
### How it works
The Chrome-free parts: the palette is one component registered into the frame-wide `shell.overlay` s
eat, rendering `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` — which is what makes it a real modal for the host'
s Escape arbitration and for background-shortcut gating. The toast is a **second** entry in the same
seat so it outlives the palette.
Taking ⌘K is the interesting part, and it writes no preference:
| Step | Mechanism |
| 1 | `ctx.shortcuts.register` refuses any default that overlaps `session.search`, and there is no u

nregister API — so the chord cannot be claimed by registering a command |
| 2 | `ctx.shortcuts.regis

terFixed` performs **no** conflict check, so a fixed binding on ⌘K is accepted |
| 3 | That fixed bi
nding makes `session.search` *conflicted*, which removes `meta+KeyK` from the Electron main process'

s natively intercepted set |
| 4 | With the chord no longer intercepted, the DOM `keydown` reaches t
he page, where fixed observers run **before** configurable dispatch — and consume it |
Steps 2–4 were verified end to end against a running app before the palette was written. A fixed bin
ding is deliberately **not user-rebindable**, which is why the plugin also registers a normal, unbou
nd command (`session.palette`) that you can attach your own chord to in Settings → Shortcuts.
The preview comes from the host's `turnOutline` projection, which already carries every turn's promp
t (≤50 code points) and response (≤120) into the session list — so for most sessions it costs **no r
equest at all**. Measured coverage was about two thirds; the rest are the sessions you have not touc
hed in a long time, and those are read lazily, one at a time, after the highlight settles.
## Compatibility
Verified against **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2** on macOS (Apple Silicon), in a real profile. The plugin depends
on the following upstream contracts, each of which was checked against the shipped bundles rather th
owing upstream contracts, each of which was checked against the shipped bundles rather than assumed:
| Contract | Where it comes from |
| `shell.overlay` as a root-scoped `list` slot with standard session hooks | `dsh-client-ui-layout`,

`dsh-client-ui-renderer`, `dsh-client-ui-session` |
| `registerFixed` / `observeFixedInput`, and fi

xed bindings being excluded from native interception | `dsh-client-shortcuts` |
| The dotted command

-id pattern (a bad id silently disables **every** keyboard command) | `dsh-client-shortcuts` |
| `ct
x.sessions.list`, `refreshProjections`, `ctx.uiWorkspace`, `ctx.workspaces` | `dsh-api-session-contr

oller`, `dsh-client-ui-workspace`, `dsh-api-workspace-controller` |
| `sessions.using` → `reference.
binding.session.rename`, and the host's "not live in this store" refusal | `dsh-api-session-controll

er`, `dsh-session-title` |
| Native interception keyed on exact chord + modifiers, unmatched chords

reaching the main frame | `lib/main.js` (`before-input-event`) |
| `turnOutline` (per-turn prompt/re

sponse previews) | `dsh-session-turn-outline` |
| `retainedBy.mainView` as "the current session" (th
e header's title span is found by its `crumbCurrent` class suffix — still `<hash>_crumbCurrent` in 0
.2.1-rc.2) | `dsh-client-ui-workspace`, `dsh-client-ui-conversation` |
Upstream may change any of these. A failure in the shortcut contract is the one to watch: it is sile
nt rather than loud.
